title: Lead removal of infrastructure, visa and safety deficits

blocks.text: Theme 3.2 · Governance and leadership · Focus area 19
Lead removal of infrastructure, visa and safety deficits

Visas, air rights, the runway and policing sit with national government, so the province leads by escalation backed with evidence, and delivers the safety programmes and basic services that are its own.
**December 2025.** Lead Removal of Infrastructure, Visa and Safety Deficits, under theme 2.1 (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64).

**October 2026: Moved.** The entry moved from supply to governance because its levers sit nationally. The stakeholder evidence, the Demand-Side barriers and MIDAS all place visas and air rights with national government; the move itself was decided at the October review [Summary of Findings, 14 Oct 2026: the deck's stated reason for the move to confirm]. The rationale holds for visas and air rights, while safety programmes are a provincial function and basic services a local one (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p58).

blocks.message: The deficits are the best-evidenced barriers in the stakeholder record, and most of the levers sit with national government or SOEs.

blocks.text: Inside communities, safety is a launch gate. Nine of the 20 shortlisted communities record a safety-perception gap and five record extortion, and the Inclusion Plan makes a formal safety assessment a separate requirement before launch (SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026, p30, p35). Congestion costs the Metro an estimated R2.8 billion a year, and water scarcity acts as a hard ceiling on visitor load in high-growth nodes (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p38).

Wesgro should run a standing escalation agenda, with each item stated as a decision, the national body that owns it and the date the province asks for, backed by market evidence. The Stakeholder Insights Report's next round already frames that evidence: the access barriers across air, visas and onward travel, and the safety issues most damaging to demand (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p14). The Diagnostic asks for dedicated tourism safety units and programmes in the Metro (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p41).

blocks.text: Kenya reduces entry friction to position Nairobi as a regional and global hub, and every comparator was scored on ease of access and visas (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p59, p11). The required change for the Western Cape, drawn from Chile, is to lobby actively for air service liberalisation and simplified visa regimes (p28).
